messages.content:
SYSTEM items:
[0] Scope decided: TV remote control only.
[1] LCD and speech recognition not included due to budget constraints.
[2] Elderly-friendly design: large buttons, standard conventions, top 10% of buttons on top for reachability, and no two-level navigation.
[3] Skip teletext option; teletext is outdated.
[4] Lighting indicators: red LED indicator and a light under the numbers and keypad that lights briefly when a button is pressed.

GOLD items:
[0] The remote will not feature speech recognition or an LCD screen.
[1] The remote will light up when a button is pressed, much like a mobile phone.
[2] Basic buttons will go on top and other buttons lower down, all on a single level.
[3] The remote will feature teletext capabilities, and the teletext buttons will be included on the main interface.
[4] The remote will use an automatic search function to find the code for the user's television brand.
[5] The remote will not have programmable favourites buttons.
[6] The remote will control only the television, replacing the earlier universal-remote decision.

messages.content:
SYSTEM items:
[0] Ambiguity on product scope (universal remote vs TV remote) raised as a problem in dialogue.
[1] Feasibility: proposed price around 25 EUR may be too high given production cost of 12.5 EUR.
[2] There is a tight timeline to get the product to market.

GOLD items:
[0] There was a misunderstanding about the target user group that forced the group to reevaluate their decisions on several components once they received the correct information.
[1] The new requirement that the remote was only to control television forced the group to change some of their initial design ideas.
[2] The group did not reach a decision on how to ensure that the remote would recognize all brands of televisions.
